question: What does the Autel EVO Max 4N do when the control link is lost, and do incident reports match?
stop_reason: claims still failing after the revision limit

intake.focus: Autel EVO Max 4N lost control link behavior
intake.reason: Question asks what the manuals/guidance say about loss of control link and what actions are taken (return-to-home/hover/land/reconnect) and whether incident reports align with those findings.

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance: when a loss of control link occurs, try to reestablish the control link and start emergency or contingency procedures if it cannot be reestablished; preflight briefings must include control link loss procedures. Autel EVO Max 4N manual: if the C2 link is lost, the drone enters a reconnection state and may return to the remote if reconnected within 10 seconds; during automatic RTH caused by signal loss, it will continue to attempt reconnect; if the link is lost more than 10 seconds, the programmed Signal Loss Action is executed, and if connection returns during RTH, RTH completes. Incident reports: unverified accounts claim total loss of control and flyaway, with RTH failures and the platform not recovered.
